2027-02-25.title: Thursday of the Second Week of Lent
readings: Cursed is the one who trusts in mortals; blessed is the one who trusts in the Lord
Happy are they who hope in the Lord
You received your good things, and Lazarus evil things; now he is comforted here, and you are in agony
2027-02-25.alt: Lenten weekday. The Alleluia is omitted throughout Lent; the Gloria is omitted except on solemnities and feasts. Liturgical colour: violet.
2027-02-25.verse: There was a rich man who was dressed in purple and fine linen and who feasted sumptuously every day. And at his gate lay a poor man named Lazarus, covered with sores,
theo: Jeremiah sets two pictures side by side. The one who trusts in mere mortals and turns his heart from the LORD “shall be like a shrub in the desert,” living in parched places where nothing good comes. But “Blessed are those who trust in the LORD, whose trust is the LORD. They shall be like a tree planted by water, sending out its roots by the stream. It shall not fear when heat comes, and its leaves shall stay green; in the year of drought it is not anxious, and it does not cease to bear fruit.” In Kerala we know such trees by the backwaters: in the hottest May they stay green because their roots reach the water. Then Jeremiah looks inside: the human heart is devious and hard to understand, but “I the LORD test the mind and search the heart, to give to all according to their ways.” Where are the roots of my heart? In money, in people's opinion, in my own strength, or in God?

Jesus answers with a story. A rich man, dressed in purple and fine linen, feasts every day. At his gate lies a poor man, covered with sores, longing for the scraps from the table; only the dogs come to him. The rich man is never said to be cruel. He simply does not see. The poor man has a name, Lazarus, which means God helps; the rich man has none. Both die. Lazarus is carried by the angels to Abraham's side; the rich man finds himself in torment and begs for a drop of water. Abraham reminds him: you received your good things in your lifetime; and between us and you a great chasm has been fixed. The chasm in eternity is the gate he never crossed in time. Then the rich man begs for his five brothers, and Abraham replies: “If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be convinced even if someone rises from the dead.” Lent asks us to open our eyes to the Lazarus at our gate, while there is still time, and to listen to the One who has indeed risen from the dead.
outline: Ask: whom do you pass every day without really seeing?
Trust in mortals or trust in the Lord.
Point 2 · The man at the gate
“Blessed are those who trust in the LORD.”
live: Notice one poor or suffering person near you today, learn their name and do something for them.
Ask in prayer: what am I really trusting in? Hand it to God.
2027-02-25.prayer: Lord God, you search the heart and know us. Root us in trust in you like a tree beside the water, open our eyes to the Lazarus at our gate, and make us listen to your word while there is time. Through Christ our Lord, who rose from the dead. Amen.
altar: At the altar the Lord sets a table for all. The Eucharist sends us out to see Christ in the poor, as the Church Fathers taught: whoever honours the Body of Christ on the altar must honour it in the poor.

quick: Those who trust in the Lord are like a tree planted by water.
The rich man's sin was that he never saw Lazarus at his gate.
Listen to God's word now; the chasm is fixed after death.
2027-02-25.action: Learn the name of one poor person you see regularly, and help them.
2027-02-25.question: Who is lying at my gate, unseen?

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a rich man who had a big feast every day. A poor man named Lazarus was hungry and sick at his gate, but the rich man never helped him. Jesus wants us to see people who need help and share with them.
family.intention: We pray for poor and hungry families near our home.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone near us who needs help? What can our family share this Lent?”

illus: A software engineer in Kakkanad walked past the same old man every morning at the bus stop. One Lenten Thursday, after hearing this Gospel, she stopped and asked his name. It was Lazar. She laughed, then cried. Now she brings him breakfast every Thursday, and he prays for her family. She says: he was at my gate for two years, and I never saw him.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you were poor for our sake. Open our eyes to the poor at our gate and root our hearts in you. Amen.
share: Blessed are those who trust in the LORD (Jeremiah 17:7). Where are my roots?
At his gate lay a poor man named Lazarus (Luke 16:20). Who is at my gate?
If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets (Luke 16:31). Am I really listening to God's word?
pm.resp: Happy are they who hope in the Lord.
interc: For the poor and the sick who lie unseen at the gates of the rich.
For the rich and comfortable, that they may open their eyes and hearts.
For those who trust only in money or power, that they may turn to God.
For farmers and all who wait for rain in the dry season.
For our group, that we may share generously this Lent.
pm.close: Father, you hear the cry of the poor. Make us see and share, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Jeremiah shows us two trees. One is a shrub in the desert: the person who trusts only in human strength. The other is a tree planted by water: blessed are those who trust in the LORD, whose trust is the LORD (Jeremiah 17:7). In the year of drought it is not anxious, and it does not cease to bear fruit.

Then Jesus tells of a rich man who feasted sumptuously every day, and at his gate lay a poor man named Lazarus, covered with sores (Luke 16:19–20). The rich man did not beat Lazarus. He did not chase him away. He simply did not see him. That was his sin.

Notice: the poor man has a name, Lazarus, God helps. The rich man has no name. In God's eyes the forgotten are remembered. After death the gate the rich man never crossed becomes a great chasm that cannot be crossed.

And Abraham says: if they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be convinced even if someone rises from the dead (Luke 16:31). Someone has risen from the dead: Jesus. Let us listen to him today, open our eyes, and cross the gate to Lazarus while there is time. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told about a rich man who had lots of food but never shared with poor Lazarus at his door. Jesus wants us to see people who need help. Can you share something with someone today?

intro: Theme: “At his gate lay a poor man named Lazarus.”
Two trees, two men, one gate, and the word that calls us while there is time.

q: Blessed are those who trust in the LORD, whose trust is the LORD. They shall be like a tree planted by water, sending out its roots by the stream.
Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust consume and where thieves break in and steal;
points.apply: Name one false security you lean on, and give it to God in prayer.

q: Those who oppress the poor insult their Maker, but those who are kind to the needy honor him.
How does God's love abide in anyone who has the world's goods and sees a brother or sister in need and yet refuses help?
points.apply: Give this week's Lenten savings directly to someone in need near you.

q: I the LORD test the mind and search the heart, to give to all according to their ways, according to the fruit of their doings.
He said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be convinced even if someone rises from the dead.’ ”
points.apply: Read one chapter of the Gospel each day this week, and act on one line of it.

concl: Trust in the Lord makes us fruitful even in drought.
Eyes opened to the poor are the beginning of eternal life.
2027-02-25.resolve: Learn one poor person's name this week and help them.
